expected_effect: Static factual election-security messages improved immediate survey confidence and accuracy in United States and Brazil experiments; whether official-source assistant grounding reduces voting-information errors or disenfranchisement is untested.
metric: Grounding accuracy; citation validity; source-conflict escalation; correction reach ratio; voting-information error rate; turnout-information error rate.
notes: The checked evidence concerns static forced-exposure messages, not assistants or real-world voting access.

expected_effect: First-page button prominence can change consent acceptance; whether a legal ban improves free and informed choice, data disclosure, political behaviour, or agency is untested.
metric: Completion and consent asymmetries; reversal or opt-out friction; comprehension; alignment with stated preferences; actual data disclosure; enforcement findings.
notes: A small interface experiment supports a bounded behavioural endpoint, not the effect of DSA enforcement or a general dark-pattern ban.

expected_effect: Forwarding labels and limits exist, but observational evidence documents substantial label non-coverage and workarounds; effects on delay, reach, virality, encryption properties, or harm remain unestimated.
metric: Reproduction number and diffusion depth; time to reach thresholds; highly-forwarded share; label coverage; coordinated sender clusters; false and true content reach differential.
notes: The checked study is descriptive and selected public political groups are not representative of WhatsApp or private chats.

mechanism_targeted: Expose voters in advance to short examples of emotional language, incoherence, false dichotomies, scapegoating and ad hominem so recognition of those taught tactics can be evaluated before campaign-content exposure.
expected_effect: Short technique-based inoculation videos improve immediate recognition of taught manipulation techniques; durability, behavioural transfer, political outcomes, pluralism, and agency effects remain unestablished.
metric: Pre-registered recognition and discernment; observed sharing behaviour; retention at 1, 4 and 12 weeks; transfer to untaught techniques; exposure and completion; heterogeneous effects; trust calibration.
notes: Established only for the bounded immediate recognition of emotional language, incoherence, false dichotomies, scapegoating, and ad hominem. Impersonation remains an unverified extension.

expected_effect: Performance-based data minimisation can reduce data available to recommenders with algorithm-, metric-, and user-dependent quality losses; effects of assistant-memory controls on manipulation or dependency are untested.
metric: Memory visibility; retained-data volume; deletion completeness; performance loss distribution; purpose changes; DPIA coverage; rights-request response time and success.
notes: The checked study used offline recommender datasets, not conversational assistants or intimate manipulation outcomes.

expected_effect: In a small 2019 IoT study, researchers received relevant personal data in three of four exercises but could not complete functional import or direct provider-to-provider transfer in any; functional assistant-state exit remains untested.
metric: Relevant-data receipt; export completeness; successful import rate; direct transfer success; switching time; percentage of useful context transferred; appeal and reversal rates.
notes: Partial Article 20 data receipt is not evidence of functional assistant-state portability or reduced lock-in.
